extracted.intended_audience: small nonprofit grantseekers and their staff; volunteer evaluators and foundation program officers
extracted.subtask_description: Using a standardized, weighted review matrix to evaluate rejected or draft grant proposals so nonprofits can self-assess and volunteer evaluators can identify promising projects to promote to funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of competing groups in the field
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an organization is aware of competing groups working in its field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This component is given higher weight in the matrix — reviewers are asked to assess whether applicants understand the landscape and how their work differs or complements others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strength of relationships to accomplish goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the organization has built strong relationships to help accomplish its goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also a higher-weight item; evaluators consider partnerships, networks, and demonstrated collaborations that increase likelihood of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanics: free of spelling and grammatical errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the proposal is free of spelling or grammatical errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is assessed but given less weight than strategic factors like landscape awareness and relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighted criteria/components
rubrics_metrics.description: The form’s components are weighted, with the components considered most important receiving more points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighting is used to reflect relative importance of different dimensions; however, the creator does not intend for proposals to be ranked solely by total scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numeric scoring per question (scale of 1 to 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluators assign points (on a scale of 1 to 3) for each question on the form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The numeric scores provide a quantitative basis, but are meant to prompt qualitative discussion rather than be the only determinant of decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer qualitative notes and follow-up availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluators are encouraged to add notes in response to each question and denote willingness to speak further with applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should read, score, and annotate proposals; nonprofits are notified of reviewers who can discuss feedback further — enabling constructive follow-up beyond a numeric score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized tool adaptable to varied proposal formats
rubrics_metrics.description: A single, standardized review tool intended to be usable across proposals that come in wildly different formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The matrix is designed so charities can use it on their own to evaluate proposals before submission; it helps bring consistent criteria to informal or varied applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of reviewers' network to promote promising organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: After evaluations are complete, the most promising organizations are distributed among the organizer’s network and promoted online; reviewers may suggest other foundations likely to support the projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is part of the outcome process: selection for added exposure and funder suggestions complements the evaluation and can lead to additional funding opportunities, including occasional personal support from evaluators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluator composition/experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are volunteer evaluators, many of whom currently work for foundations (the Unfunded List used a team of about 30 such evaluators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The use of experienced foundation staff as reviewers is an implicit quality standard: feedback comes from people familiar with funder expectations and decision-making.
